description:
Hi, I'm Explorer! 🚀

I believe the best ideas come when we dare to think beyond limits. I love exploring new things, trying new experiences, and turning curiosity into innovation.

I'm currently in my exploring phase — learning, experimenting, and figuring out how technology can actually make a difference.
summary:
GREEN is a voice-first mobile web app that helps small farmers decide which crop to plant next, then act on that decision in the same place. It is designed to read real NASA POWER data (temperature, rainfall and soil wetness for the farm’s location, compared with the previous ten years) and turn it into plain advice with a spoken guide. GREEN ranks suitable crops for the coming season, compares them with the farmer’s current crop, and explains the evidence, benefits, risks and information gaps behind each suggestion. It supports, never replaces, local expertise.

Farmers often avoid new crops because they cannot see the cost, the market or who will harvest. So GREEN adds a cost and profit calculator, nearby mandi (Market) distances with transport costs, and booking of machines, workers and trucks.

This matters because heat, uncertain rain, falling water and tired soil threaten livelihoods, yet NASA’s data never reaches the field. GREEN is a working prototype: NASA POWER data is live; prices, providers and costs are sample estimates; SMAP, MODIS and GRACE are planned next.

Note: This project is built in only two to three days. I did not have enough time to review it as thoroughly as I would have liked, although I checked as much as I could. The main purpose is to present an idea and make it concrete. To turn the idea into designs, code, images and documentation, I used ChatGPT, Figma Make, Meta AI, Claude and Gemini.
details:
What it does and how it works

GREEN is a voice-first mobile web app that helps a farmer choose the next crop and act on that choice. The farmer signs up by speaking or typing, shares location, and picks the crop currently in the field by photo or voice search. GREEN then reads NASA POWER data for that location (temperature, rainfall and root-zone soil wetness) and compares the last three months with the same months of the previous nine years. A transparent rule-based scoring engine ranks crops that fit the coming season (rabi or kharif) using this dryness and heat signal, each crop’s water need, heat tolerance, soil benefit (for example nitrogen-fixing legumes and deep roots), estimated profit and the farmer’s own priority (save water, earn more, or soil health). The existing crop is shown alongside the recommendations. Each suggestion explains its evidence, benefits, risks and information gaps. After choosing, the farmer sees an editable cost and profit calculator, nearby mandis with distance and transport cost, a how-to-grow voice guide, and can contact and book machines, workers and trucks.

Benefits

It turns scientific satellite data into plain advice in Urdu and English, with a spoken guide. It removes the fears that stop farmers from trying better crops: who will harvest, where to sell, and what it will cost. Low-water and soil-building options are surfaced first.

Intended impact

Less water use, healthier soil, steadier income, and more confident decisions for small farmers. Because NASA POWER covers the whole Earth, the same approach can be localized to other regions by changing the crop table and market data. A future phase adds village collection points and trucks to balance supply between villages.

Tools and technology

HTML, CSS and vanilla JavaScript; NASA POWER REST API; Web Speech API for voice input and speech output; hand-drawn SVG charts of NASA data; a progressive web app (installable, caches the last NASA result); a database layer designed for Supabase (Postgres, row-level security, anonymous auth) with an optional Edge Function for a natural Azure Urdu voice; Figma Make for the clickable prototype. The work was done on a laptop and runs on any smartphone browser. AI tools (ChatGPT, Meta AI, Claude and Figma Make) helped turn the idea into designs, code and documentation.

Creativity

GREEN treats the real obstacle as practical, not only informational: advice is useless without workers, machines, a market and a price. It is built for low literacy (voice-first, photo selection, a dictionary that understands local names such as Chawal, Chol and Munji), and it is honest by design: it states data limits, shows no advice when NASA data cannot be read, and labels demo values.

Factors considered

Farmer literacy, language and weak connectivity; the roughly 50 km resolution of NASA POWER, which is regional rather than field-level; seasonal fit; privacy (no ID numbers collected, each user sees only their own data); the need for local agronomists to validate crop rules; and that GREEN supports, never replaces, farmer judgment and local expertise.

Note:

This project is built in only two to three days. I did not have enough time to review it as thoroughly as I would have liked, although I checked as much as I could. The main purpose is to present an idea and make it concrete. To turn the idea into designs, code, images and documentation, I used ChatGPT, Figma Make, Meta AI, Claude and Gemini. Prices, providers and costs are sample estimates, and SMAP, MODIS, GPM and GRACE-FO are planned next.
